# Dynamic Redlining Benefits

Working Note: Dynamic Redlining Benefits

Over the past month, I’ve been digging into how our dynamic redlining feature impacts legal contract review cycles. Initial observations confirm that automating change tracking significantly speeds up the process. In our pilot with the Procurement Dept, review times dropped from an average of 5.2 days to 2.8 days per contract—a 46% improvement. Lawyers report fewer back-and-forths since every edit is automatically highlighted and contextualized, reducing miscommunication.

Error rates also appear to decline. Our QA audits found that contracts processed with dynamic redlining had 30% fewer overlooked changes compared to manual reviews. This suggests the tool not only speeds things up but also improves accuracy.

Open questions remain around edge cases, such as how the system handles simultaneous edits from multiple users on deeply nested clauses. We also want to measure the impact on downstream teams, like compliance and finance, which might spot issues earlier now.

Next steps: coordinate with the UX team to refine multi-user editing flows, and set up analytics to track end-to-end contract lifecycle times across teams. Gathering quantitative data will help us build a stronger business case for wider rollout.
